checks.text: On initial load, the page displays the heading "Sudoku Puzzle", a select labelled "Difficulty" with "Easy" selected, a button labelled "New Game", and a timer display showing "00:00".
Clicking the button "New Game" generates a new board where the first cell (row 1, column 1) contains a non-zero digit, and the timer resets to "00:00".
With a new game active, clicking the cell at row 1, column 1 (which contains a pre-filled digit) and then clicking the button "1" does not change the cell's value, as pre-filled cells are locked.
With a new game active, clicking an empty cell at row 1, column 2 and then clicking the button "5" changes that cell's text to "5".
After entering a valid number in an empty cell, the timer display updates to show a non-zero value, such as "00:01" after one second has passed.
Clicking the select labelled "Difficulty" and choosing "Hard" then clicking "New Game" generates a board with fewer pre-filled digits than the "Easy" board, specifically at least 30 empty cells.
When all 81 cells contain valid digits 1-9 with no duplicates in any row, column, or 3x3 box, the page displays the text "Puzzle Solved" and the timer stops updating.
If a user enters a digit that creates a duplicate in the same row, the cell border turns red and the text "Invalid move" appears below the grid.
Reload keeps the current board state: after entering "5" in row 1, column 2 and reloading the page, the cell at row 1, column 2 still displays "5" and the timer continues from the last saved value.
